results.title: Bulacan dike construction in full swing, completion set early 2027
results.description: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is speeding up work to fix and finish dikes in Bulacan, including a 1.8‑kilometer stretch along the Bagbag River in Barangay Calizon, Calumpit that has long been exposed to flooding. DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said P576 million has been allocated for the project, with strict oversight from design to bidding and construction to ensure completion by early 2027. He noted that with contractors involved in past anomalies now facing charges, the agency must address unfinished projects that left communities vulnerable. The issue gained national attention after President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. revealed that some flood control structures had either not been completed or not built at all despite full payment. The disclosure intensified scrutiny of former contractors and placed DPWH under pressure to restore both infrastructure and public trust. Workers are tasked with sealing missing sections, reinforcing damaged areas, and ensuring the dike functions as part of Bulacan’s flood protection system. Calumpit Mayor Glorime “Lem” Faustino said the municipal government will take the lead in monitoring and evaluation to improve coordination with DPWH, a step she noted was missing in the past. Residents, still wading through thigh‑deep muddy floods in Barangay Calizon, raised a pressing concern: whether the dike will be finished before another major flood causes damage.
